title: Future study and career plans after 4th of ESO
grammar: Will, going to, future continuous, and future perfect

vocab.example: I want to get a university degree.
She is doing a summer internship.
He won a scholarship to study abroad.
Which university do you want to attend?
I sent my job application yesterday.
She chose a career path in science.
Communication is an important skill.
Do you have the right qualifications?
Teaching is a noble profession.
My long-term goal is to become a doctor.
There are many opportunities for career advancement.

student.repte: Plan your future! Think about what you want to study and what career you want to pursue.

products.desc: A 150-word text outlining future study/career plans, integrating at least three future tenses and course vocabulary.
A 2-3 minute presentation detailing personal future career interests and how they plan to achieve their goals.

teacher.repte: Students explore future educational and professional trajectories, developing vocabulary and structures to express hypotheses and plans.
teacher.methodology: Task-Based Learning (TBL), Collaborative Learning, Inquiry-Based Learning (career research), Self-Regulation & Peer Evaluation.
teacher.assessment: 5.1 (Clarity, coherence, and original content without plagiarism).

title: Migration, what if... ?
grammar: Zero, first, second, third, and mixed conditionals

vocab.example: Language is one of the main migration challenges.
There are many misconceptions about immigrants.
We must fight against racism.
Classism creates social divides.
Current political trends affect migration laws.
Cultural clashes can happen when adjusting to a new country.
People migrate for many different reasons.
The emotions of leaving home are complex.

student.repte: Step into someone else's shoes. Understand the journey, challenges, and emotions of migration.

products.desc: A creative, three-scene theatrical script and performance: 'Before Leaving', 'Once in the New Country', and 'Resolution'. Must feature all conditional types and a narrator.
Post-performance class discussion on the moral and hidden social messages of the skits.

teacher.repte: Develop empathy and social awareness regarding global migration through role-play and debate, utilizing complex conditional structures.
teacher.competencies: Ciutadana (CC1 - social identity & empathy), Llengua Estrangera 3 & 5.
teacher.methodology: Cooperative learning, dramatic role-play, empathy-focused moral discussions.
teacher.assessment: Observation of empathy, accurate use of conditionals, oral fluency in debate.

title: Health and Well-Being
grammar: Modals for giving advice and expressing necessity (should, could, must)

vocab.example: Healthy food gives you energy.
Good nutrition is essential for growth.
Sleeping 8 hours is a good lifestyle habit.
Take care of your mental health as well as your body.
Regular exercise makes you stronger.

student.repte: Become a wellness expert! Create guides and give advice on how to live a healthier physical and mental life.

products.desc: A single digital slide deck or infographic built around a main 'How to...?' question and three sub-questions. Modal-based advice is dynamically hidden and revealed.
A doctor-patient or coach-athlete spoken diagnostic scenario recorded for peer feedback.

teacher.repte: Promote healthy habits and metacognitive reflection on personal well-being, practicing modals of advice.
teacher.competencies: Personal, social i d’aprendre a aprendre (CPSAA 5 - metacognition & habit improvement), Digital (CD1).
teacher.methodology: Project-based learning (infographics), peer-feedback loops, scenario-based role-play.
teacher.assessment: Accuracy of modals, visual communication (digital competence), spoken fluency.

title: Life Paths
grammar: Reported speech (tense backshifting) and reporting verbs (promised, refused, suggested)

vocab.example: Everyone has different life paths.
Overcoming personal challenges makes you resilient.
Graduating was one of her greatest achievements.
Phrases like 'afterwards' and 'prior to'.

student.repte: Discover inspiring stories around you. Interview someone whose life path inspires you and share their journey.

products.desc: A short, engaging presentation supported exclusively by images. Students tell the interviewee's story and reflect on how it inspires them.
A side-by-side list comparing direct interview questions with their reported speech transformations.

teacher.repte: Practice narrative reporting and descriptive skills by synthesizing and relaying real-life inspirational interviews.
teacher.competencies: Emprenedora (CE2 - evaluating personal strengths), Llengua Estrangera 3 & 5.
teacher.methodology: Interview-based inquiry, narrative storytelling, visual presentation techniques.
teacher.assessment: Correct application of reported speech backshifting, oral presentation skills without text reliance.

title: Job Interview
grammar: Question formation (yes/no, wh- questions, formal indirect questions), professional register

vocab.example: I saw several job advertisements online.
A good professional cover letter is essential.
Follow standard CV conventions.
Use action verbs like 'managed' or 'created' in your CV.

student.repte: Get ready for the real world! Create your professional profile and experience a real-life job interview simulation.

products.desc: An individual applicant portfolio consisting of one modern CV and one tailored, formal cover letter.
Collaborative simulation where student recruiters conduct and audio-record formal interviews with candidates.

teacher.repte: Simulate a professional recruitment cycle focusing on formal register, direct questioning, and active listening.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 3.4 (discourse strategies, turn-taking, managing communication challenges).
teacher.methodology: Simulation/Role-play, peer recruitment, formal writing practice.
teacher.assessment: Formality of register, accuracy in question formation, interaction strategies.

title: CSI - Relative Clauses
grammar: Defining and non-defining relative clauses (who, which, that, where, whose)

vocab.example: Detectives use deductive reasoning to solve cases.
The area was secured with crime scene tape.
They found several clues in the room.
The fingerprints are crucial evidence.
They created suspect profiles based on the testimonies.

student.repte: Become a detective! Invent a crime mystery and challenge your classmates to solve it using clues.

products.desc: A single presentation slide displaying twelve picture-only clues with absolutely no text.
A short narrative connecting all clues using accurate relative clauses and identifying the culprit.
An interactive classroom round where the team projects their clue board and fields classmates' questions.

teacher.repte: Consolidate the year's grammar (questions, reported speech, modals) through a capstone deductive reasoning project.
teacher.assessment: Mastery of relative clauses, ability to field unscripted questions, narrative cohesion.
